page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the ESv4 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, yielding 2 threads per core. It features 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1D cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate that the E2s_v4 exhibits modest compute and memory performance. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1405.58 and multi-core performance scored 1844.46. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show 102.76 GB/sec for cached small blocks, dropping to 14.18 GB/sec for read-only and 11.28 GB/sec for write operations on large uncached blocks. Geekbench testing yielded an average single-core score of 1268.0, but a lower multi-core score of 1521.0. Cryptographic and database operations also registered in the lower tiers, with a PassMark database score of 726.39 and Redis SET operations reaching 1.76 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E2s_v4 provides a high memory density per vCPU, making it a viable entry-level option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing. Due to its limited CPU core count and lower multi-core benchmark ratings, it is best suited for lightweight database hosting, basic caching layers, or small-scale enterprise applications where RAM capacity is prioritized over raw compute throughput.
